metadata.title: Amon-Ra St. Brown - Logs full practice Thursday
metadata.description: St. Brown (ankle) practiced in full Thursday.
metadata.analysis: Head coach Dan Campbell told Richard Silva of The Detroit News on Monday that St. Brown tweaked his ankle during this past Sunday's win against the Packers, and while the wide receiver sat out Wednesday's session, he was able to handle a full workload one day later, fulfilling Campbell's prediction. St. Brown thus should be good for the 11.3 targets per game that he's averaged through six appearances this season Sunday versus the Vikings.

metadata.title: Amon-Ra St. Brown (ankle) practices Thursday
metadata.description: Amon-Ra St. Brown practiced on Thursday.
metadata.analysis: Brown was not seen during the open portion of practice on Wednesday. His return on Thursday is a good sign for his status for Sunday's game against the Vikings.

metadata.title: Amon-Ra St. Brown - Returns to practice Thursday
metadata.description: St. Brown (ankle) returned to practice Thursday, Colton Pouncy of The Athletic reports.
metadata.analysis: Head coach Dan Campbell gave some key players a day off Wednesday, with St. Brown among them. The star wideout is practicing the following day. If St. Brown manages to practice without limitations, he'll eliminate any remaining doubts about his availability for Sunday's game against the Vikings.

metadata.title: Amon-Ra St. Brown Back on the Practice Field on Thursday
metadata.description: Detroit Lions wide receiver Amon-Ra St. Brown (ankle) was back at practice on Thursday after he was a non-participant on Wednesday, according to The Athletic's Colton Pouncy. St. Brown came out of the Week 7 win over the division-rival Green Bay Packers with some ankle soreness, but after returning to practice on Thursday, the Lions expect him to be fine for their upcoming game on Sunday at home against the division-rival Minnesota Vikings. The 27-year-old was most likely just being rested for maintenance purposes on Wednesday in the team's first practice of the week. Fantasy managers should expect the four-time Pro Bowler to be a full-go this weekend, and he will be a must-start in all fantasy leagues despite the tough matchup against the Vikings. The Sun God did not appear to be slowed by his ankle on Sunday against Green Bay, catching nine of 11 targets for a season-high 153 yards. It was St. Brown's second 100-yard game of 2026, and he enters Week 8 action as the WR4 in half-PPR scoring with 46 catches for 525 yards and five touchdowns on 68 targets through only six games played. The Sun God leads all receivers in points who have played only six games this year.

metadata.title: Amon-Ra St. Brown - Sits out Wednesday's practice
metadata.description: St. Brown (ankle) didn't practice Wednesday.
metadata.analysis: St. Brown logged a typical 78 percent snap share during this past Sunday's win against the Packers, reeling off nine catches for 153 yards on 11 targets in the process. On Monday, head coach Dan Campbell told Richard Silva of The Detroit News that St. Brown tweaked his ankle in that contest but should practice by Thursday. As a result, St. Brown's absence Wednesday doesn't come as a surprise, and he should mix into drills in some capacity Thursday.

metadata.title: Amon-Ra St. Brown Absent From Wednesday's Practice
metadata.description: Detroit Lions star wide receiver Amon-Ra St. Brown (ankle) is still dealing with an ankle injury and did not practice on Wednesday, according to The Detroit News' Nolan Bianchi. St. Brown apparently tweaked his ankle in Sunday's Week 7 win over the division-rival Green Bay Packers, but the 27-year-old still played 78% of the offensive snaps and had a big game for his fantasy managers, catching nine of his 11 targets for 153 yards. The 27-year-old is now on the Week 8 injury report, but the expectation is that he will return to practice on Thursday and be ready to play in Sunday's divisional showdown against the 6-0 Minnesota Vikings in Week 8. The Sun God is a must-start in all fantasy football lineups when he is active. He has exactly 11 targets in each of the last three games and has seen double-digit targets in five of six games, catching 46 total passes on 68 targets for 525 yards and five touchdowns, which makes him the WR4 overall in half-PPR scoring, behind only Jaxon Smith-Njigba, CeeDee Lamb, and Christian Watson.

metadata.title: Amon-Ra St. Brown - Nursing ankle issue, should play Week 8
metadata.description: Lions head coach Dan Campbell said that St. Brown tweaked his ankle during Sunday's 20-17 win over the Packers but should be ready to practice Thursday, Richard Silva of The Detroit News reports.
metadata.analysis: Campbell is planning for St. Brown to rest during the Lions' first Week 8 session Wednesday, but the star wideout should be able to practice during the subsequent two days to put himself on a path to play Sunday against the undefeated Vikings. The ankle injury likely explains why he saw a slight decline in playing time -- he logged 53 of 68 offensive snaps (78 percent) -- but St. Brown still  delivered for fantasy managers in the win over Green Bay. Though he was held out of the end zone for the third game in a row, St. Brown finished with nine receptions for a season-high 153 yards.

metadata.title: Amon-Ra St. Brown Dealing With Ankle Injury
metadata.description: Detroit Lions wide receiver Amon-Ra St. Brown (ankle) tweaked his ankle in Sunday's Week 7 victory over the division-rival Green Bay Packers, according to Richard Silva of The Detroit News. The plan is for the Lions to let St. Brown sit out of practice on Wednesday before he returns on Thursday. St. Brown was not really slowed down by his ankle in the 20-17 win on Sunday, as he caught nine of his 11 targets for a season-high 153 yards against Green Bay. As long as he returns to Thursday's practice, St. Brown should be just fine to play in Week 8 against the division-rival Minnesota Vikings, where he would be a must-start WR1 in fantasy leagues despite the tough matchup against one of the best defenses in the NFL. St. Brown played only 78% of the Lions' offensive snaps on Sunday, but the slightly reduced playing time did not hurt his production at all. The 27-year-old four-time Pro Bowler has had exactly 11 targets in each of the last three games and has not seen double-digit targets in just one of his six games so far in 2026. After his big game against Green Bay, St. Brown is the WR3 overall in half-PPR scoring with 46 catches on 68 targets for 525 yards and five touchdowns so far this year.

metadata.title: Amon-Ra St. Brown leads team in receiving Sunday
metadata.description: Amon-Ra St. Brown hauled in 9-of-11 targets for 153 yards in Sunday's 20-17 win over the Green Bay Packers.
metadata.analysis: The veteran wideout played very well on Sunday. He led the team with 153 receiving yards over the course of the afternoon, although he wasn't able to get into the end zone to put the cherry on top. Fantasy managers should continue to regard him as a top-tier option moving forward.

metadata.title: Amon-Ra St. Brown - New season high in receiving yards
metadata.description: St. Brown caught nine of 11 targets for 153 yards in Sunday's 20-17 win over the Packers.
metadata.analysis: The 153 yards were a new season high for St. Brown, topping the 142 yards he amassed against the Bills in Week 2. The star wideout's touchdown drought grew to three games, but his 46-525-5 line on 68 targets through six games this season remains elite. St. Brown will face a tough test in Week 8 against the dominant defense of the undefeated Vikings.

metadata.title: Amon-Ra St. Brown Sets New Career High in Week 7
metadata.description: Detroit Lions wide receiver Amon-Ra St. Brown was unstoppable during Sunday's Week 7 matchup against the Green Bay Packers. The stud wideout had no issues torching this secondary all game long. He hauled in nine of his 11 targets for 153 yards in the win. The 153-yard performance is a new career-high for Brown, topping his 142-yard performance from Week 2. The Lions continue to feed St. Brown the ball with 33 targets over his last three games. Fantasy managers should expect his numbers to take a hit next week against a tough Minnesota Vikings defense. St. Brown is still a strong WR1 despite a tough matchup in Week 8.

metadata.title: Amon-Ra St. Brown Should See Heavy Target Volume in Week 7
metadata.description: Five games into his 2026 season, Detroit Lions wide receiver Amon-Ra St. Brown has recorded 37 catches for 372 yards and five touchdowns on 57 targets. The 26-year-old's production has slowed down a little bit lately, as he's failed to crack 75 receiving yards in a game and has hauled in just one touchdown catch since Week 2. In Week 7, Detroit will host the Green Bay Packers. The game projects to be a high-scoring affair, but the Packers have fielded a stingy pass defense so far this season, ranking third in the NFL in yards per pass attempt allowed (6.0) and eighth in passing touchdowns allowed (seven). Still, St. Brown is averaging nearly 12 targets per game this year and has been the clear number one option in the passing game for Lions quarterback Jared Goff. St. Brown remains a high-end WR1 option for fantasy managers in Week 7.

metadata.title: Amon-Ra St. Brown racks up 69 yards Sunday
metadata.description: Amon-Ra St. Brown caught 6-of-11 targets for 69 yards in Sunday's 45-21 win over the Arizona Cardinals.
metadata.analysis: The star wideout had an okay game on Sunday. He racked up 69 yards in an easy win over the Cardinals, but he wasn't able to get into the end zone at all, which left him with a mediocre fantasy total to his standards. He has had a great start to the season overall and should continue to be a high-end fantasy option moving forward.

metadata.title: Amon-Ra St. Brown - Six catches in Week 5 win
metadata.description: St. Brown secured six of 11 targets for 69 yards and committed two fumbles that remained with Detroit in the Lions' 45-21 win over the Cardinals on Sunday.
metadata.analysis: St. Brown fell below his usual lofty standards with his numbers, but the star receiver still finished with team-high reception and target totals while also slotting in as the runner-up in receiving yards. St. Brown remains as integral a component of the Lions' air attack as ever, as he now has back-to-back 11-target games and has already seen 57 passes come his way overall in the first five contests of the campaign. St. Brown has turned those opportunities into a 37-372-5 line, and he'll be looking to snap a two-game touchdown drought when the Lions return to action in a NFC North home clash against the Packers on Sunday, Oct. 25, following a Week 6 bye.

metadata.title: Amon-Ra St. Brown Could Be Poised for Massive Game in Week 5
metadata.description: Across four games in 2026, Detroit Lions wide receiver Amon-Ra St. Brown has recorded 31 catches for 303 yards and five touchdowns on 46 targets. The 26-year-old currently ranks as the WR3 in overall PPR scoring and the WR4 on a per-game basis. In Week 5, St. Brown and the Lions will take on the Arizona Cardinals. Arizona has had major issues defending the pass so far this season, allowing 11 touchdown receptions through four games and ranking dead last in the NFL in yards per pass attempt allowed (9.1). The Lions have also shown a tendency for playing high-scoring, pass-heavy games, as their defense has allowed at least 30 points in three out of four games and quarterback Jared Goff is currently averaging over 40 pass attempts per game. Between the matchup and the state of the Detroit defense, St. Brown remains a clear high-end WR1 option for fantasy managers in Week 5.

metadata.title: Amon-Ra St. Brown makes eight grabs in Week 4 loss
metadata.description: Amon Ra St. Brown came up with 8-of-11 targets for 75 yards in Sunday's 32-26 loss to the Panthers.
metadata.analysis: St. Brown failed to make it four straight games with a touchdown to start the season, but he still produced a solid showing. St. Brown has largely delivered for fantasy managers over the first quarter of the season, averaging nearly eight receptions for more than 75 yards with five scores to this point. He remains a certain WR1.

metadata.title: Amon-Ra St. Brown - Eight catches in Week 4 loss
metadata.description: St. Brown secured eight of 11 targets for 75 yards in the Lions' 32-26 loss to the Panthers on Sunday night.
metadata.analysis: St. Brown was essentially as busy as usual in the air attack, although he was in the relatively rare position of finishing second in targets, and to tight end Sam LaPorta at that. Nevertheless, the star wideout tied with LaPorta for the team lead in receptions, and St. Brown's yardage tally was his second-highest figure through the first four games. Despite the disappointing team-level outcome, St. Brown's fantasy outlook is as bright as customary heading into a favorable Week 5 road matchup against the Cardinals next Sunday.

metadata.title: Amon-Ra St. Brown Remains a High-End WR1 Option in Week 4
metadata.description: Detroit Lions wide receiver Amon-Ra St. Brown had a quiet game by his lofty standards in Week 3, recording four catches for 19 yards and a touchdown on eight targets against the New York Jets. However, the 26-year-old is still off to an excellent start to the season, as he's hauled in 23 receptions for 225 yards and five touchdowns on 35 targets across three games. In Week 4, St. Brown and the Lions will go on the road to take on the Carolina Panthers. The Panthers have been tough to throw on so far in 2026, allowing the fifth-fewest yards per pass attempt (6.1) in the NFL. However, Carolina placed starting cornerbacks Jaycee Horn (quad) and Mike Jackson (groin) on Injured Reserve on Wednesday. Particularly if the Lions' defense continues to struggle and Detroit is forced to turn to the air, St. Brown could be well-positioned to have a big day. Even coming off the down week, St. Brown remains a must-start WR1 option for fantasy managers in Week 4.

metadata.title: Amon-Ra St. Brown finds the end zone in Week 3 win
metadata.description: Amon-Ra St. Brown caught 4-of-8 targets for 19 yards and a touchdown in a 31-24 win over the Jets.
metadata.analysis: St. Brown was not able to capitalize on his eight targets, but was able to help salvage the day with a touchdown in the second quarter. St. Brown now has five touchdowns through the first three games of the season and will look to build on a strong start to the season against the Panthers in Week 4.

metadata.title: Amon-Ra St. Brown - Salvages day with TD in Week 3 win
metadata.description: St. Brown caught four of eight targets for 19 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 31-24 win over the Jets.
metadata.analysis: The star wideout tied Jaymyr Gibbs to lead the Lions in targets, but St. Brown did little with his volume aside from a four-yard TD strike from Jared Goff in the second quarter. It was still St. Brown's fifth score of the season in three games, to go along with 23 catches for 228 yards on 35 targets. He'll likely get plenty of looks from Goff again in Week 4 on the road against the Panthers.

metadata.title: Amon-Ra St. Brown Scores a Touchdown in Otherwise Quiet Day
metadata.description: Detroit Lions wide receiver Amon-Ra St. Brown recorded four receptions for just 19 yards (4.8 yards per catch) and a touchdown in a 31-24 victory over the New York Jets in Week 3. St. Brown did see eight targets on the day, which was tied for the team high, but he wasn't able to produce much outside of his four-yard touchdown. Running back Jahmyr Gibbs led the Lions in receptions on the day with seven, while Isaac TeSlaa led the team in receiving yards with 66 (one more than Gibbs). While the touchdown saved the day in Week 3, fantasy managers don't have much to worry about with St. Brown moving forward. Through three games, St. Brown has tallied 35 targets, 23 receptions, 228 receiving yards, and five touchdowns. He remains a high-end WR1 moving forward.

metadata.title: Amon-Ra St. Brown Remains a Top Wide Receiver Option in Week 3
metadata.description: Detroit Lions wide receiver Amon-Ra St. Brown has gotten off to a dominant start to the 2026 season, recording 19 catches for 209 yards and four touchdowns on 27 targets across his first two games played. The Lions have been forced into pass-heavy game scripts because of their struggling defense, and St. Brown remains the clear number one option in his team's passing game. In Week 3, the Lions will host the New York Jets. The Jets have been tough to pass on so far this season, ranking second in the NFL in both total passing yards (285) and yards per pass attempt (4.7) allowed. While that adds an element of uncertainty to St. Brown's outlook, the 26-year-old has been one of the most reliable target-earners in fantasy football in recent seasons. All in all, St. Brown profiles as a must-start WR1 for fantasy managers in Week 3.

metadata.title: Amon-Ra St. Brown scores twice in loss Thursday
metadata.description: Amon-Ra St. Brown caught 6-of-8 targets for 142 yards and two touchdowns in Thursday night's 41-31 loss to the Buffalo Bills.
metadata.analysis: St. Brown was on fire on Thursday night. He had a slow start, but he ended up finishing the game with a team high in receptions and receiving yards while finding the end zone twice against the Bills. He will continue to be a top-tier fantasy option moving forward, especially in PPR scoring formats.

metadata.title: Amon-Ra St. Brown Posts Another Monster Game in Week 2
metadata.description: Detroit Lions wide receiver Amon-Ra St. Brown was one of the lone bright spots in his team's 41-31 Week 2 loss to the Buffalo Bills, recording nine catches for 142 yards and two touchdowns on 13 targets. St. Brown has gotten off to a fantastic start to the season, hauling in 19 receptions for 209 yards and four touchdowns on 27 targets across Detroit's first two games. The 26-year-old has been a highly reliable wide receiver for fantasy managers for a number of years now, posting three consecutive seasons with at least 115 catches, 1,250 receiving yards, and 10 touchdowns coming into 2026. Still, he could be poised for a career season from a production perspective if the Lions' defense continues to struggle as mightily as it has through the first two weeks. Heading into Detroit's Week 3 matchup against the New York Jets, St. Brown profiles as a high-end fantasy WR1.

metadata.title: Amon-Ra St. Brown - Stellar numbers in Week 2 loss
metadata.description: St. Brown brought in nine of 13 targets for 142 yards and two touchdowns in the Lions' 41-31 loss to the Bills on Thursday.
metadata.analysis: The Lions played from behind all night, which had a role in St. Brown seeing massive volume on his way to game-high figures in receptions, receiving yards and targets. The star wideout recorded both his scoring grabs in the second half, capping off Detroit's opening drive of the third quarter with a two-yard touchdown and then providing the final points for either side when he hauled in a 27-yard strike from Jared Goff with 1:42 remaining. St. Brown has opened the season in signature fashion with consecutive two-TD tallies, and he'll next take aim at the Jets defense on the fast track of Ford Field on Sunday, Sept. 27.

metadata.title: Amon-Ra St. Brown Could Be Set Up for Another High-Volume Game
metadata.description: Detroit Lions wide receiver Amon-Ra St. Brown was one of the key performers in his team's Week 1 win over the New Orleans Saints, recording 10 catches for 67 yards and two touchdowns on 14 targets. While it wasn't St. Brown's most efficient game, he earned five more targets than any other Lions pass-catcher and was heavily involved in Detroit's red zone attack. In Week 2, St. Brown and the Lions will travel to Buffalo to take on a Bills defense that allowed 274 passing yards and two passing touchdowns to the Houston Texans this past Sunday. With the high-powered Bills offense likely to move the ball against the banged-up Lions secondary, Detroit could operate with a pass-heavy game script on Thursday night. The Lions will also be missing three starters on the offensive line, which may lead to plenty of short and intermediate-area targets for St. Brown. The 26-year-old profiles as a high-end WR1 option for fantasy managers in Week 2 against the Bills.

metadata.title: Amon-Ra St. Brown hauls in 10 receptions in Week 1 win over Saints
metadata.description: Amon-Ra St. Brown hauled in 10 of his team-leading 14 targets for 67 yards and two touchdowns in the Lions' 31-30 Week 1 win over the New Orleans Saints.
metadata.analysis: St. Brown was dynamic in the season-opening contest for head coach Dan Campbell, hauling in both of quarterback Jared Goff's touchdown passes in the win. The wideout remains an elite WR1 option in all formats ahead of a Week 2 road matchup against the Buffalo Bills.

metadata.title: Amon-Ra St. Brown - Finds end zone twice in OT win
metadata.description: St. Brown caught 10 of 14 targets for 67 yards and two touchdowns in Sunday's 31-30 overtime win over the Saints.
metadata.analysis: The star wideout got the new season started with a bang, leading Detroit in catches, targets and receiving yards while connecting with Jared Goff for a 19-yard score in the third quarter and a four-yard strike in overtime. The latter proved to be the winning TD when New Orleans failed on a two-point attempt on its answering touchdown. St. Brown has scored double-digit TDs in three straight seasons, and he may be well on his way to doing so again. He'll look to make an impact again in Week 2 on the road against the Bills.

metadata.title: Amon-Ra St. Brown has contract restructured by Lions
metadata.description: The Lions restructured the contract of WR Amon-Ra St. Brown.
metadata.analysis: LT Penei Sewell also had his contract restructured. The Lions created $35.68 million in cap space.

metadata.title: Amon-Ra St. Brown - Contract restructured by Detroit
metadata.description: The Lions and St. Brown agreed to a restructured contract Saturday, Adam Schefter of ESPN reports.
metadata.analysis: Per Spotrac, $26 million of St. Brown's salary was converted into a signing bonus, which alone created $20.8 million in cap space to give the Lions more flexibility for the next two seasons. St. Brown has been one of the most productive receivers since being selected by the Lions in the fourth round of the 2021 NFL Draft, having logged 100-plus catches and 1,000-plus receiving yards in each of the last four years. He finished the 2025 regular season with 117 catches (on a career-high 172 targets) for 1,401 yards and 11 touchdowns across 17 games. He'll once again lead a Lions pass-catching group that also includes Jameson Williams, Isaac TeSlaa and Sam LaPorta.

metadata.title: Lions Restructure Amon-Ra St. Brown's Deal
metadata.description: The Detroit Lions restructured the contracts of wide receiver Amon-Ra St. Brown and left tackle Penei Sewell on Saturday to create over $30 million in salary cap space, according to Adam Schefter of ESPN. With St. Brown's restructure, $26 million of his salary was converted into a signing bonus, which created $20.8 million in cap space for the next two seasons. The 26-year-old has been a Pro Bowler in each of the last four seasons with the Lions, catching a ridiculous 457 of his 623 targets for 5,340 yards and 39 touchdowns in 66 regular-season starts. He has recorded 1,000 receiving yards in the last four seasons as well, while finding the end zone double-digit times in each of the last three years. St. Brown caught 117 of his 172 targets for 1,401 yards and 11 touchdowns in 17 starts in 2025, and he is one of the safest fantasy football wideouts in the league as he enters his sixth season in 2026 with a Week 1 matchup at home against the New Orleans Saints.

metadata.title: Amon-Ra St. Brown a Must-Start Wide Receiver in Week 1
metadata.description: Detroit Lions wide receiver Amon-Ra St. Brown has established himself as one of the most reliable pass-catchers in the NFL, recording three consecutive seasons with at least 115 catches, 1,250 receiving yards, and 10 touchdowns. Entering 2026, St. Brown once again profiles to be the lead target-earner in a Lions passing game that projects to be a dangerous unit. In Week 1, Detroit will host the New Orleans Saints. The Saints fielded an underrated pass defense in 2025, allowing the fifth-fewest total passing yards (3,336) and 12th-fewest yards per pass attempt (6.8) in the NFL. However, the Lions' passing offense finished ranked third in total passing yards last season, and St. Brown projects as a strong bet to see 8-10 targets on Sunday. Heading into the season opener, St. Brown profiles as a high-end WR1 option for fantasy managers.
